correctness.rationale: For all connected simple orientations, the cofactor identity, augmented incidence Schur complement and Cauchy–Binet prove the exact oriented spanning-unicycle formula. Tree coordinates show each surviving minor is precisely signed cycle imbalance; matrix-tree and orthogonal cycle projection give the spectral equivalent. Complete-graph covariance is a scalar-minus-rank-one operator. Karamata majorization of tournament scores proves the sharp transitive maximum square norm; degree parity proves the sharp regular/near-regular minimum and explicit constructions attain every endpoint. All boundaries and normalizations are spelled out. Pure-Python fraction-free checker passed 172 exact graph cases and all 1096 tournaments of orders 3–5 plus all 32768 six-vertex score extrema. Those checks corroborate but do not replace the general proof.

originality.rationale: The closest directed-root-polytope primary papers establish the vertex representation, rank/dimension and Ehrhart dissections, not the present population vertex-covariance determinant and all-spanning-unicycle squared integer-discrepancy sum. A publicly established single-cycle imbalance-volume formula is expressly subsumed and credited, not presented as standalone new work. Full-text comparison of same-object directed-root sphere papers found only different metric optimizers. A net signed-graph matrix-tree formula uses different incidence data. The all-graph identity plus sharp orientation-extremizing tournaments is not implied by the compared statements, with residual generic incidence-minor literature risk.
residual_risks: The determinant of an augmented incidence matrix may have appeared as an unstated equivalent special case of general matrix-minor or optimal-design theory, not identified in focused searches.
The existing single-cycle squared-imbalance relation is prior mathematical content, not a newly claimed standalone invariant.
Self-review does not constitute independent external novelty or correctness validation.

value.rationale: The theorem identifies an intrinsically defined, equal-vertex-mass Euclidean covariance determinant for directed edge polytopes throughout the whole connected simple-graph class; graph orientation matters despite identical underlying edges and root norms. The exact weighted unicycle sum has a structural graph interpretation and detects precisely the rank transition. The tournament restriction solves a natural extremal roundness question completely with explicit equality cases, an all-orders covariance spectrum, and sharp condition number growth approaching three; it is not a one-off finite enumeration or mere implementation of a standard exercise. The square-score bound alone is established combinatorics and credited, while its precise covariance and unicycle consequences are the new synthesis.
